newsitem.title: UK: Brady bonds strong but risks profit-taking - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds strong but risks profit-taking - dealers.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices held firm on Wednesday after the strong overnight rally after the Federal Reserve announced it would not change U.S. interest rates, traders said.
But they also said there was likely to be some profit-taking.

"Volumes are up and there are signs of confidence that the market remains attractive to investors and it looks as though the general bias is going to be up," Salomon Brothers emerging markets research analyst David Boren said.
"But there has been some profit-taking as well," he added.
"I would think that there is especially going to be a lot of interest in Russia."
Russian debt prices posted powerful gains, amid good fundamental news and a renewed government commitment to economic reform.
Many market players had expected a 25 basis point hike in U.S. interest rates. The absence of a policy shift led Brady bond trade into a frenzy of relief buying.

However U.S. analysts said the surge in prices might not be sustainable because the underlying conditions -- concerns that a strong U.S. economy and low unemployment would lead to higher U.S. rates during the summer.
Brazilian "C" bonds led the charge in the U.S., storming 1-1/4 higher to 77-1/4 bid in late afternoon trade, but were even higher on Wednesday afternoon at 78-3/4 bid.
The strength was also due to the announcement of Brazil's offer to swap Brady bonds for 30-year global bonds or cash, dealers said.
Argentine FRBs gained 3/4 to 93, and were 1/8 up at 93-1/8 bid on Wednesday, while discount bonds rose 1-1/8 to 84-7/8 and were last bid at 86.

"Everything is up and away. The Fed didn't tighten and this has triggered a fairly substantial move and from the short-end floaters into the long-end fixed," Richard Gray BankAmerica analyst Richard Gray said.
"But there is some risk of profit-taking," he added. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7718.
